I'm mapping the blue and red marker positions: blue on right column 16, red markers in the bottom row at columns 2, 6, and 11. Comparing to the earlier example, each red marker at the bottom seems to trigger the line segment to shift up by one row, so I need to trace segments accordingly between the marker columns.

Now I'm building out a 12x17 grid, filling in each row's column ranges based on these shifting segments — row0 covers columns 3-6, row1 covers 7-11, row2 covers 12-16 plus 0-2, and so on down through row10, tracking how each chain of segments repeats with the row offset.

seg4 r5 cols0-2 completes that chain, confirming it checks out.

I'm mapping the blue and red marker positions to figure out the line-drawing rule: lines start at blue columns/rows and shift direction (up or right) whenever they cross a red-marked row or column, similar to the pattern in the example grid.

I'm working through the pattern now: each blue line splits into three segments, shifting up one row each time it crosses a red marker's column, so segment1 stays at the original row, segment2 shifts up one row starting at the red column, and segment3 shifts up another row after the second red column. Checking each row confirms this cascading pattern holds consistently across all three blue lines.

Filling in the remaining shifted columns for each row band, keeping the fixed 2s at column 0 for rows 3 and 7, giving a final grid width of 17.
